Referred Sections: CMM-601.4: Initial Primary Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF)

Required findings: Symptoms must include BOTH a clinically significant daily pain level causing functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing) AND unremitting radicular pain to the shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity resulting in disability.

Physical examination must demonstrate ANY of the following: dermatomal sensory deficit, motor deficit (e.g., biceps or triceps weakness), reflex changes, shoulder abduction relief sign, nerve root tension sign (e.g., positive Spurling's maneuver), or unremitting radicular pain without concordant objective findings.

Imaging must include plain cervical spine X‑rays (including flexion/extension lateral views) AND MRI/CT showing neural structure compression at the requested level(s) that is concordant with symptoms and exam, caused by herniated disc(s), synovial/arachnoid cyst, central/lateral/foraminal stenosis, or osteophytes.

Conservative management must have failed to provide clinically meaningful improvement, with at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated): prescription‑strength analgesics/steroids/gabapentinoids/NSAIDs for six weeks; a provider‑directed exercise program for six weeks; epidural steroid injection(s) or selective nerve root block(s) at the same level(s).

General criteria: absence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders, and documented nicotine‑free status (never‑smoker or abstinent from all nicotine products for ≥6 weeks prior to surgery, verified by objective cotinine testing).

Symptoms must include ANY of the following: upper or lower extremity weakness, numbness, or pain; fine motor dysfunction (e.g., difficulty buttoning, handwriting, clumsiness of hands); gait disturbance; new‑onset bowel or bladder dysfunction; or frequent falls.

Physical examination must demonstrate ANY of the following: abnormal grip‑and‑release test, ataxic gait, hyperreflexia, Hoffmann sign, Babinski sign, tandem walking ataxia, inverted brachial radial reflex, increased muscle tone or spasticity, clonus, or a myelopathic hand.
MRI or CT must show findings concordant with the individual's symptoms and exam and be caused by either cervical spinal cord compression or cervical spinal stenosis.

Non-Indications: Procedures performed for indications other than radiculopathy or myelopathy, or performed without meeting ALL of the listed criteria, are considered not medically necessary.
Important criteria & exceptions: Nicotine‑free status must be verified by objective cotinine testing (serum, urine, or saliva) if the patient is not a never‑smoker.
A minimum six‑week trial of appropriate conservative therapy (pharmacologic and/or physical therapy) is required before surgery for radiculopathy.
Plain cervical spine X‑rays with flexion/extension views are required for radiculopathy cases.
Absence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders is required for radiculopathy; not explicitly required for myelopathy per policy.
Imaging must be performed at the level(s) of proposed surgery and must demonstrate pathology that correlates with clinical findings.
Documentation required: Detailed clinical note documenting symptom severity, functional impairment, and disability.
Objective physical examination findings as listed for the specific indication.
Imaging reports: cervical spine X‑rays (including flexion/extension) and MRI/CT showing concordant pathology.
Records of conservative management attempts (medication list, duration, physical therapy notes, epidural steroid injections or nerve blocks).
Psychosocial assessment confirming absence of unmanaged mental/behavioral health disorders.
Nicotine‑free verification: smoking history statement and cotinine test result (if applicable).
